files_opened: research/corpus/primary/koskenniemi_parpola1979.pdf (rendered with PyMuPDF at two pixels per point: pages 20 and 21 for the sign chart; pages 39, 64 and 84 as wider areas for samples 4, 14 and 30; and the numbered-field boxes on pages 28, 39, 48, 53, 54, 64, 68, 77, 79, 84, 87, 90, 92, 95, 99 and 101; images only, no text layer)
notes: I read all 40 assigned rows (sample_index 0 to 39) and recorded 156 drawn units in total. Every row has a single physical line: I looked at the source crop of each row for unnumbered continuation lines above and below the numbered line and found none, so each proposed printed_line_crops list (numbered line only) matches the actual membership. I identified signs by comparing each unit with the position-chart cards and, for the narrow hatch patches and the parallel-line signs, by measuring ink positions in the exact crops (five pixels per point) against cards scaled at about 3.95 pixels per point (calibrated from sign heights of matching glyphs). The 597/598 hatch patches were assigned by the gap to the neighbouring sign or underline: a patch lying about two points before the next cell supported the right-edge code (598), and a patch lying about two points after the previous cell's end supported the left-edge code (597); both codes remain in the shape-only list. In samples 14 and 20 a pair of narrow patches separated by 2.7 to 2.8 points matches card 762 as one cell, but two adjacent cells 598 then 597 would give the same ink and a unit count of 2; I kept the one-cell reading and recorded the alternative. Pairs and triples of parallel lines are separated only by about 0.3 to 0.4 point of spacing between cards: samples 8, 10 and 25 favour 765, 765 and 769 over 9, 9 and 543, while samples 10 (second triple), 30, 31 and 32 are kept as sets (766 with 10, and 770 with 424) because the source spacing falls within the variation between gaps of one sign. Sample 3 unit 6 is an oval with a slashed small oval that matches the interior of 700 but lacks 700's underline; I left its strict set empty and listed 700 as shape-only. Sample 35 contains an isolated high tick that I coded 23 (no underline) with 258 as the shape-only alternative because 258 is underlined and slightly longer. Crop judgments: sample 21 is marked incorrect because about 0.4 point of ink from the next numbered line lies in the bottom two pixel rows of the exact crop, and sample 30 is marked incorrect because the two left corner ticks of its first unit lie 0.6 to 1 point outside the crop (found by comparing the source crop's ink columns with the crop window). Samples 14, 18, 22, 23, 24 and 36 are judged correct with observations about empty margins or a speck. Convention difficulties: deciding whether a very small isolated mark is a unit (sample 14 ring about 1.2 points wide, treated as a speck; sample 35 tick, treated as a unit), and whether widely spaced signs in the same line are one unit sequence (samples 30 and 39, where I did not infer a boundary from the gap). The printed digit 1 in the field is drawn like a dotted i in some rows; I recorded it as 1. Exposure: none. I opened only the files listed, did not open any prediction, frame or pipeline file, any other reader's folder, the earlier evaluation references, the row-verification pilot or the PDF text layer, and I did not open anything under data/raw other than my own scratch folder. The scratch folder data/raw/2026-10-07-helsinki1979-digitization/reader-tmp-v3-B1/ is deleted at the end of the run. A listing of the top level of BLIND showed only page-count-source, position-chart and the sample files.
